# ---------- Narrator: ElevenLabs reads Gemini's commentary aloud ----------
# Every clip is saved in data/narration/ (named by a fingerprint of voice + text),
# so the same sentence is only paid for once.
NARRATION_DIR = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "narration")


@app.post("/api/narrate")
def narrate():
    key = os.environ.get("ELEVENLABS_API_KEY")
    voice = os.environ.get("ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID")
    model = os.environ.get("ELEVENLABS_MODEL", "eleven_flash_v2_5")   # flash = fast and cheap
    if not key or not voice:
        return jsonify(error="ELEVENLABS_API_KEY / ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID missing in .env"), 503
    text = " ".join(str((request.get_json(force=True) or {}).get("text", "")).split())[:400]
    if not text:
        return jsonify(error="no text"), 400

    os.makedirs(NARRATION_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    name = hashlib.sha256(f"{voice}|{model}|{text}".encode()).hexdigest()[:32] + ".mp3"
    path = os.path.join(NARRATION_DIR, name)
    if os.path.exists(path):                                   # already made → free
        return send_from_directory(NARRATION_DIR, name, mimetype="audio/mpeg")
    try:
        r = requests.post(
            f"https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice}",
            params={"output_format": "mp3_44100_128"},
            headers={"xi-api-key": key, "Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "audio/mpeg"},
            json={"text": text, "model_id": model,
                  "voice_settings": {"stability": 0.6, "similarity_boost": 0.75}},   # calm, steady narrator
            timeout=20,
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
    except Exception as e:
        detail = getattr(getattr(e, "response", None), "text", "") or ""
        return jsonify(error=f"ElevenLabs: {e} {detail[:200]}".strip()), 502
    tmp = path + ".part"                                       # write then rename → never a half-saved file
    with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
        f.write(r.content)
    os.replace(tmp, path)
    return Response(r.content, mimetype="audio/mpeg")

The narrator is built, but it can't talk yet: ElevenLabs rejected your API key with "401 Invalid API key". The key in `.env` is formatted correctly, so it's probably been revoked or mistyped. To fix it, make a new key on the ElevenLabs website, paste it into `.env` as `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and restart `python app.py`. I haven't heard it play over the music yet, so check the volume once the key works.

**How it works**
- **Server, [app.py](app.py):** a new `/api/narrate` endpoint sends the text to ElevenLabs and gets back an mp3. It saves each clip in `data/narration/`, named after the voice and the exact text, so the same sentence is only paid for once. It uses ElevenLabs' fast, cheap "flash" voice model by default.
- **Browser, [static/main.js](static/main.js):** when a phrase starts using Gemini's plan, `narrate(plan)` reads out Gemini's commentary sentence at 45% volume over the music.
  - Only one clip plays at a time. If a clip is still playing when the next phrase starts, that phrase's commentary is skipped, not queued, so the narrator never falls behind the music.
  - Each plan is only spoken once.
  - Pausing, or switching the 🎙 Narrator button off, stops the voice.
- **If ElevenLabs fails:** the music never waits for the narrator. On any error it shows "Narrator unavailable — music continues" under the panel and tries again 30 seconds later.
- **Button:** "🎙 Narrator: on/off" sits next to "🎼 Hide score" in [static/index.html](static/index.html). It starts switched on.

**What I tested**
- With a pretend ElevenLabs, two identical requests made only one paid call (the second came from the saved file), errors came back cleanly, and empty text was refused.
- Both files pass a syntax check.
- The one real request failed with the bad-key error above.

content.text:
The 📚 Gallery button is in the panel, Replay works, and it's committed as `07042a1`. I tested it in headless Chrome against a throwaway copy of the server holding one fake saved performance; your real saves and MongoDB weren't touched.

**What it does**
- **📚 Gallery** opens a panel in the middle of the screen, styled like the Score panel. ✕, Esc or the button again closes it.
- **Each card shows:**
  - the title
  - when it was saved
  - the date the music was at
  - the "view from" currency
  - the seating as coloured instrument → currency pairs, including added musicians (muted ones are dimmed, removed ones are left out)
  - the first Gemini headline, in quotes
- **"⏳ waiting to upload"** marks performances that are only saved on your laptop.
- The top line says whether the list came from MongoDB or only from your laptop.
- **▶ Replay** closes the gallery, sets "View from", restores every seat (instrument, currency, muted, removed) and any added musicians, jumps to the saved date and starts playing. If a saved currency isn't in the loaded data, it keeps the current seat and says so in the status line.
- Titles are shown as plain text, so a name typed into the save box can't break the page.

**Test result:** with a fake save that had a removed horn, a muted piano and an extra harp on SEK, Replay brought all of them back. It switched the view to USD, played from June 2016, and was still playing 3 seconds later with no errors.

**Two things to know:**
- **Not tried with real saved performances.** You have none yet, and MongoDB was unreachable from this Wi-Fi during the test. Save one, open the gallery and press Replay once to check.
- **Replay's status message disappears quickly.** The orchestra's "loading instruments" message overwrites it if the music wasn't already playing. The "📚 Replaying …" note on the stage still shows.

I also added a short description of the gallery to [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) and ticked its to-do item. The code is in [static/main.js](static/main.js), under the new `GALLERY` section.

## How to work with the developer (read this every session)
The developer is building this solo at DurHack 2026 (deadline 12:00 Sun 15 Nov, feature freeze 09:30). Explain changes in plain English and keep code readable with short comments.
1. Before changing anything, say in 2–3 plain-English lines what you'll change and why. If a request is ambiguous, pick the most sensible reading, say which one you picked, and go ahead.
2. Keep the design rules in this file: classical-sounding music (chords, cadences, voice-leading), every note explainable in the Score panel, changes must feel musical (never sudden volume jumps), main view = line graph, at least one musician always stays.
3. Make small, safe changes. Never break: music playback, the Gemini conductor (with maths fallback), the ElevenLabs narrator, ECB auto-loading, MongoDB saving (with the offline queue), Gallery/Replay, keyboard shortcuts, volume sliders.
4. After editing, check your work: `node --check static/main.js`, `python -m py_compile app.py`, and if possible a quick simulation of the music loop so nothing throws errors.
5. Never print or commit secrets (.env, atlas-credentials.env). Never call paid APIs in loops without caching.
6. When done, explain simply what changed and how to test it at http://localhost:5050, and update this file if anything important changed.
7. Then commit with a clear message and push, so the session is linked in Entire (the Entire CLI captures Claude Code sessions as checkpoints on commit).


## The project: **"Curren-Sing"** (currency + sing)
Built for DurHack 2026, theme **COMPOSITION** (mix art, music and tech; judged on Creativity & Innovation · Technical Execution · Research & Learning · Polish).

Each world currency is an instrument in an orchestra. **Default seating** (user can change it in the "Orchestra seating" panel — any currency in the file → any instrument):
| Currency | Instrument | Role |
|---|---|---|
| USD | Violin | main melody |
| GBP | Cello | long chord notes |
| JPY | Flute | off-beat answers |
| CHF | Harp | arpeggio, up if rising / down if falling |
| EUR | Piano | chords on beats 1 & 3 |
| AUD | Trumpet (replaced the too-quiet French horn) | enters when tense |
| CAD | Double bass | foundation |
| (world) | Timpani, deep drum | appear only when the world is stressed |

ECB rates are "per 1 EUR", so `prepare()` converts every currency (plus EUR itself) into **strength vs a basket** (USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, CHF, AUD, CAD, geometric mean) — that's how EUR can be an instrument. All currencies with ≥70% coverage are kept (gaps filled with last value) and are selectable.

### How the music is composed (classical engine — every note must be explainable)
- **Conductor** picks a *character* per 4-bar phrase: Pastorale · Cantabile · Misterioso · Agitato · Grandioso → key (C major / A harmonic minor), tempo marking (Adagio…Presto), dynamics (p…ff), chord progression (e.g. I–IV–V–I, i–iv–V–i). **Gemini decides this** via `/api/analyse` (asked mid-phrase, applied at the next phrase); maths fallback (`fallbackDirection`) when offline. `sanitizeDirection()` validates Gemini's JSON.
- **One chord per bar**, phrases end in cadences. Instruments: violin melody & flute answer = strong beats land on a chord tone near where the currency sits in its 3-month range (max leap 7 semitones), weak beats move one scale step towards it; cello holds 3rd/5th with smooth voice-leading; double bass plays root/5th; piano = Alberti bass when calm, repeated chords when tense; harp arpeggio up/down with the currency's trend; trumpets when tense; timpani tuned to tonic & dominant; deep drum only in Grandioso. (In code the trumpet part is still called `horn` / `HN`; old saves that say "French horn" are mapped to Trumpet in `instByLabel`.)
- **Gemini reads ahead**: `prefetchAI()` keeps asking Gemini about the data rows where the next 1–3 phrases will start (one request at a time), storing plans in `S.aiCache`; `onBar` uses the plan for the current phrase start if present, else maths. Cache is cleared on new data / view change. Server (`app.py`) tries GEMINI_MODEL then GEMINI_FALLBACK_MODELS from `.env` (currently gemini-3.5-flash-lite first; 3.8-flash was overloaded), skipping busy (429/503) models instantly, 15 s timeout, thinkingLevel "low". `gemini_test.py` diagnoses keys/models/latency.
- **Narrator (ElevenLabs)**: when a phrase starts with a Gemini plan, `onBar` calls `narrate(plan)` → POST `/api/narrate` {text: plan.say (Gemini's commentary)} → plays the mp3 via an HTML `Audio` over the music (volume from the narrator slider, default 45%). Server caches each clip in `data/narration/` (sha256 of voice|model|text) so repeats cost nothing; model default `eleven_flash_v2_5` (override with ELEVENLABS_MODEL). Rules: one clip at a time (new ones are *skipped*, not queued, while one is busy), each plan spoken once, stops on pause / when 🎙 Narrator is turned off, 20 s timeout, on any failure it waits 30 s and shows "Narrator unavailable — music continues" in `#narrStatus`. The music never waits for it.
- **📚 Gallery** (button in the panel → centred `#gallery` panel, Esc/✕ closes): `openGallery()` loads GET `/api/performances` ({items, mongodb}); each card (`galleryCard`) shows title, saved date, music date, view, seating (instrument → currency, guests included, muted dimmed, removed hidden), first Gemini headline, and a "⏳ waiting to upload" badge for items with `local: true` (saved on the laptop while MongoDB is unreachable). "▶ Replay" → `replayPerformance(p)`: applies its view, restores `S.voice`/`S.assign`/`S.removed`/`S.muted` for the 7 seats and `S.extra` guests (matched by instrument label & currency name; anything not in the loaded data is skipped and named in the status), `jumpToDate(p.at)` (shared with the "Jump to" menu), then starts playing. All saved text is HTML-escaped (`esc`).
- `S.why[k]` stores the note + plain-English reason; the **Score panel** (right side, toggle "🎼 Hide score") shows conductor choice, progression, current chord, and each instrument's note + reason.
- Keep it classical: functional harmony, voice-leading, cadences — not free-scale noodling.

- **Guest musicians (“+ Add musician”)**: `S.extra` (max 8) — user picks any instrument type + any currency. `playGuests()` keeps the vibe unchanged: quiet velocity, chord notes only, fixed gaps in the bar (melody guests beats 2/4 off-beats, low guests every other bar, colour guests pos 3/7), take turns when >3. Drawn as dashed lines; listed in the Score panel; saved with performances. Volume sliders: narrator volume + music volume (Tone.Destination).

- **Keyboard**: Space = play/pause, ←/→ = 3 months back/forward, Shift+←/→ = 1 year (ignored while typing in an input/select). Esc closes the Gallery.

Design rules (keep them):
- **Each melody follows its currency's value** (up → higher notes).
- **A currency "not in a good place"** (far from its ~1-year normal and/or more volatile than usual, `S.cur[c].stress`) is **gently** louder (max +6 dB, eased per bar).
- **Changes must feel musical, never like turning up the phone volume**: drama comes from (a) a **sudden accented note (sforzando)** when a currency makes a surprising move (`z` vs its last-60-day volatility > 3.2, with a cooldown), shown as "⚡ USD jolts — Violin"; (b) **new instruments entering** (trumpet → timpani → deep drum) as world tension rises, with hysteresis; (c) key change major↔minor with hysteresis; (d) tempo gliding slowly 70→130 bpm. World tension `S.Ws` is smoothed per bar (0.12).
- **"View from" menu**: default = the world basket; or pick any currency → every currency is re-measured in that currency (`applyView(b)`, recomputes `S.cur` from `S.raw`), the chosen one becomes a flat line. Graph + music follow the view; world tension stays basket-based.
- **World condition** = average stress of ALL currencies (ranked 0–1) blended 50/50 with **Gemini's** judgement.
- **Main view = line graph** of every seated currency (% change over the last ~2 years, lines coloured by instrument, pulse on notes) + world-tension area chart underneath + whole-history overview with playhead.
- Purpose: *sonification* — hear the state of world markets; accessibility; early awareness.

Data is **loaded automatically**: `GET /api/ecb` in app.py downloads the ECB zip, extracts it to `data/eurofxref-hist.csv` (gitignored), refreshes at most every 12 h, falls back to the cached copy; `loadECB()` in main.js calls it on page load and via the "🌍 Latest ECB" button. "Load CSV" and "Demo data" still exist.
Data: **European Central Bank daily reference rates** (rates per 1 EUR, 1999 → today), `eurofxref-hist.csv` from https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist.zip — put it in `data/`. File is newest-first and has `N/A` values — `parseCSV()`/`prepare()` already handle that. Demo moments: 2008 crash, Euro crisis 2011, **Brexit vote June 2016**, COVID March 2020, 2022 (the "Jump to" menu).

## Code layout
```
app.py              Flask server (port 5050 — macOS AirPlay uses 5000)
                    /api/ecb          → latest ECB rates (downloaded, cached 12 h in data/)
                    /api/analyse      → Gemini judges world tension → {mood 0-1, headline, commentary}
                    /api/narrate      → ElevenLabs text→speech mp3, cached in data/narration/<hash>.mp3
                    /api/performances → save/list performances in MongoDB Atlas (db "hackathon"),

static/index.html   page + control panel
static/main.js      data → stress/world maths → Tone.js orchestra → p5.js stage visuals
static/style.css
static/assets/      (sound files if needed)
test_db.py          MongoDB connection test

atlas-credentials.env  MONGODB_URI (secret, gitignored)
.env                GEMINI_API_KEY, GEMINI_MODEL, GEMINI_FALLBACK_MODELS, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY,

.venv/              Python venv (flask, pymongo, python-dotenv, requests)
```
Run: `source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && python app.py` → http://localhost:5050 (opening index.html directly works but has no AI/saving).

### Important technical lessons

content.text:
I replaced the trumpet with a clarinet that plays all the time, and you can now click or drag the timeline at the bottom to jump to any date. Both worked in a browser test. They're committed and pushed (`6fdafba`).

**Clarinet instead of trumpet (still on AUD)**
- The trumpet wasn't really quiet. It only played when the world was tense or AUD was in trouble, so most of the time it was silent.
- The clarinet plays all the time. It holds a soft middle note from the current chord, changing every half bar, between the cello and the violin.
- In tense music it plays on every beat and louder, so tension changes how it plays, not whether you hear it.
- Old saved performances that say "French horn" or "Trumpet" replay as Clarinet.

**Draggable timeline**
- The history strip at the bottom of the screen is taller now. Click anywhere on it, or drag the yellow handle, to go to that date.
- It shows years every 5 years, small red dots for the famous moments (2008, Brexit, COVID…), and a date bubble when you hover or drag. When the mouse isn't on it, it shows a "drag to move through time" hint.
- Clicks on the side panels don't move the timeline.
- Fast dragging used to fire a burst of "⚡ jolts" from every date it passed through, so those are switched off while you drag.
- The year marks are worked out once when the data loads, not on every frame, to stay clear of the freezing problem noted in CLAUDE.md.

**Tested** in headless Chrome with the real ECB data:
- The clarinet samples loaded and it played on every bar.
- Clicking at 25% of the strip jumped to 2005, and dragging to 70% landed in 2017.
- The music kept playing with no errors.

I couldn't hear the audio in the test, so listen once to check the clarinet's volume next to the others. If it's too loud or soft, tell me and I'll change the clarinet's `gain` value (now −8) in [static/main.js](static/main.js#L24).

To try it, restart the server (`python app.py`), open http://localhost:5050, press Play and drag the strip at the bottom. [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) now covers both changes.
